name: Diaphragmatic (Belly) Breathing
steps: Place one hand on chest, one on belly
Inhale through nose: belly should expand (not chest)
Exhale through nose or mouth: belly falls
Practice for 5-10 minutes, twice per day
benefits: Lowers heart rate and blood pressure
best_time: Any time; especially useful during stress or before sleep

name: Anulom Vilom (Alternate Nostril Breathing)
steps: Sit upright in a comfortable position
Close left nostril with ring finger; open right
This is ONE cycle. Repeat 10-15 cycles
benefits: Balances left and right brain hemispheres
cautions: Avoid if you have a severe nasal blockage or cold
Do not hold breath if you have high blood pressure (just flow through)
best_time: Morning or evening on empty stomach

research.author: Sharma et al.
research.finding: Reduced perceived stress and improved cardiovascular parameters

name: Bhramari (Bee Breathing)
steps: Sit upright in a comfortable position
Close ears with thumbs, place fingers over eyes (Shanmukhi Mudra) or just close eyes
Exhale while making a continuous humming sound ('mmmmm') like a bee
Feel the vibration resonating in the head
benefits: Lowers blood pressure and heart rate
best_time: Any time; especially effective before bed or during anxiety

research.author: Kuppusamy et al.
research.finding: Reduced blood pressure and heart rate in participants

name: Box Breathing (Sama Vritti)
progression: Increase to 5-5-5-5, then 6-6-6-6 as capacity improves
benefits: Used by Navy SEALs for performance under pressure
cautions: If 4 seconds feels too long, start with 3-3-3-3
Avoid breath holds if pregnant or have uncontrolled blood pressure
best_time: Before stressful situations (presentations, meetings, exams), during acute stress, any time focus is needed

name: 4-7-8 Breathing (Modified Pranayama)
benefits: Extended exhale activates parasympathetic nervous system
cautions: May cause lightheadedness initially; practice seated or lying down
If 7-second hold is too long, scale down proportionally (e.g., 2-3.5-4)
best_time: In bed before sleep, or any time to calm down quickly
developer: Developed by Dr. Andrew Weil based on pranayama principles

name: Kapalbhati (Skull-Shining Breath)
strokes: Start with 30 strokes, then rest. Build to 60-120 strokes per round
steps: Take a passive inhale (belly expands naturally)
Perform a FORCEFUL, short exhale through nose (belly pulls in sharply)
Allow the inhale to happen passively and naturally
Start with 30 strokes per round, rest between rounds
Build up to 60-120 strokes per round over weeks
best_time: Morning, on empty stomach. Never after meals.
